extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task
extraction.description: A dataset for language-independent named entity recognition covering English and German. It focuses on four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations and miscellaneous entities. The dataset includes training, development, test, and unannotated data files for both languages.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For training and development sets, ten days' worth of data were taken from files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, texts were from December 1996. The German data was extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. Training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. Named entity tagging was done by hand at the University of Antwerp following mostly MUC conventions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English raw data from Reuters Corpus consisting of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997, covering the month of September 1996 (17 million tokens). German raw data from ECI Multilingual Text Corpus extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau, taken from the months of September to December 1992 (14 million tokens).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 - December 1996 for annotated data, September 1996 for raw data. German: End of August 1992 for annotated data, September - December 1992 for raw data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging was done by hand following mostly MUC conventions. Four entity categories were used: three standard categories plus a MISC category for names not in other categories, including adjectives like Italian and events like 1000 Lakes Rally.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were at the University of Antwerp
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: English data was preprocessed with memory-based MBT tagger for POS tagging and chunking. German data was preprocessed with Treetagger decision tree tagger for lemmatization, tagging and chunking.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains person names and locations as named entities
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development/tuning, and testing for named entity recognition systems
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, chunking, and lemmatization were applied. English data was processed using memory-based MBT tagger for tagging and chunking. German data was processed using Treetagger for lemmatization, tagging and chunking.

name.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition.

description.evidence: The shared task of CoNLL-2003 concerns language-independent named entity recognition. We will concentrate on four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations and names of miscellaneous entities that do not belong to the previous three groups.

publisher.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task

The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus3... extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus2. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus3.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus2. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997... The preprocessed raw data covers the month of September 1996... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus3... extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau... The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992. The unannotated data contain 17 million tokens (English) and 14 million tokens (German).

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: For the training and development set, ten days' worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, the texts were from December 1996. The preprocessed raw data covers the month of September 1996... All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories. This includes adjectives, like Italian, and events, like 1000 Lakes Rally, making it a very diverse category.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Named entities are phrases that contain the names of persons, organizations and locations. Example: [ORG U.N. ] oﬃcial [PER Ekeus ] heads for [LOC Baghdad ]

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The learning methods were trained with the training data. The development data could be used for tuning the parameters of the learning methods... the method could be trained on the training data and tested on the test data.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: for all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. We created two basic language-speciﬁc tokenizers for this shared task. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).
